paper_metadata.title: The influence of individual socioeconomic status on the clinical outcomes in ischemic stroke patients with different neighborhood status in Shanghai, China

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population, recruitment period, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it is a single-center retrospective study. While the flow of participants is described, the high number of excluded patients (121 not meeting requirements, 104 refused, 27 missing data) from the initial screen of 723 suggests potential selection bias, as those who refuse or have missing data may differ socioeconomically from those enrolled.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (SES) is measured using a multi-dimensional, pre-specified scoring system tailored to the Chinese context. The components (education, income, occupation, insurance) are clearly defined and applied consistently to all participants.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The personal SES of each patient was evaluated using a summed score derived from his or her educational level, household income, occupation, and medical reimbursement rate.
items.reasoning: The components and scoring system (0-4 for each) are explicitly detailed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Each factor was categorized to five groups from low to high level, for which a gradually increasing score (0-4) was assigned
items.reasoning: The use of a composite score is a standard approach in SES research, and the categories are objective.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: We divided the study population into three groups according to the tertiles of score distribution (Figure 1): Low (≤7), Middle (8-9), and High groups (≥10).
items.reasoning: The use of tertiles is a standard, non-data-dependent method for grouping scores.
